canonical_statement: For every positive Euclidean dimension n and nonnegative real exponents p and q satisfying 1 <= p and 1/q = 1/p - 1/n, there is a constant C depending only on n, p, and q such that every compactly supported C1 real function on R^n has Lq norm at most C times the Lp norm of its Frechet derivative.
domain_and_universes: n : Nat; p q : NNReal; u : EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n) -> Real; proposition in Prop
ordered_binders: q^-1 = p^-1 - n^-1 after coercion to Real
conclusion: eLpNorm u q volume <= C * eLpNorm (fderiv Real u) p volume
statement_selection: The repository gloss 'Sobolev embedding in norm form' and the intake scope select the classical first-order compact-support Euclidean estimate. The formal target fixes real scalar values, C1 regularity, Lebesgue volume, operator norm of the Frechet derivative, and a uniform existential constant. A source-page and historical-attribution audit remains downstream; it cannot silently revise this statement.
degenerate_cases: Dimension zero is excluded. The p = 1 endpoint is included. The conjugacy equation plus q in NNReal excludes p >= n in any satisfiable instance; no redundant p < n premise is added. Compactly supported zero and other boundary functions remain included.
